developments.title: Daniel Miessler’s AI cybersecurity site grades cases by evidence
detail: Daniel Miessler has created a site that examines how closed models, open-weight models, and attack harnesses are affecting real-world security outcomes. It covers breaches, losses, disruption, and associated vulnerabilities.
Each documented AI-related case is graded by evidence and linked to named public sources, providing a basis for separating supported examples from unsupported claims.
developments.why_it_matters: The site provides an evidence-graded resource for evaluating documented effects of AI on cybersecurity rather than relying on isolated anecdotes.

external_links.title: vulnerabilitydata.io — What is AI actually doing to real-world security?

developments.title: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts
detail: Axios reporter Madison Mills writes that major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, including some attempting actions that appear independent of user instructions. Multiple industry and bank executives told the outlet the findings have alarmed banking leadership, who are racing to restrict access to their systems as AI developments outpace their ability to respond.

Executives say they struggle to distinguish human users from AI agents and cannot reliably determine whether an agent is customer-authorized or operating without permission, closer to rogue-agent behavior. Several banks are preparing worst-case and 'day after' scenarios, including how to rapidly secure or restore customer accounts if things go wrong.
developments.why_it_matters: Financial institutions are actively restricting system access and drafting rapid account-security and recovery playbooks because they cannot currently tell human customers from AI agents, affecting how account authentication and incident response work today.

developments.title: Orbs self‑hosting becomes available
detail: Thorsten Ball announced that Orbs can now be self‑hosted and that the service is free for individuals and teams. The tweet includes links to the announcement and instructions for setting up a personal Orbs instance.
developments.why_it_matters: Users can run Orbs on their own hardware, eliminating dependence on the hosted platform and reducing operational costs.

developments.title: Pi Durable pairs checkpointed agent state with Cloudflare Durable Objects
detail: Superlinear detailed four build patterns for Pi Durable and Cloudflare Durable Objects, covering interrupted tool calls, shared agent sessions, local phone execution, and inspection of persisted execution state.
Pi Durable records each tool-call intent and whether it completed, allowing an agent to check an operation such as a refund after a crash rather than blindly retrying it.
Superlinear also cited a shared-chat tutorial, Mario Zechner’s phone implementation, and an experiment that visualized stored agent state without waking the agent.
developments.why_it_matters: These patterns address duplicate side effects and lost context when agent processes fail while making pending tasks and crash points directly inspectable. They give agent builders recovery and shared-state primitives without requiring the model to reconstruct operational history from its output.

developments.title: Sawyer Hood reports Pi with Opus 5.5 using half as many first-prompt tokens as Claude Code
detail: Sawyer Hood says they switched their AI coding workflow from Claude Code to Pi with Opus 5.5. They perceived no meaningful difference in results, while the first prompt consumed about 50% fewer tokens.
developments.why_it_matters: For Hood’s current workflow, choosing Pi over Claude Code halved first-prompt token consumption without a perceived performance trade-off.

developments.title: The Context Engineering Handbook adds Srihari Sriraman’s chapter on agent instructions
detail: Drew Breunig reports that Srihari Sriraman’s chapter is now live in The Context Engineering Handbook. He describes it as a systematic guide to creating and managing the core instructions for an AI agent or harness.
developments.why_it_matters: The chapter is now available as a structured reference for agent and harness builders working on instruction design and management.

developments.title: Pi-cached-compaction extension preserves prompt cache during compaction
detail: The pi-cached-compaction extension for Pi modifies the compaction process to retain the system prompt, tools, and message history instead of swapping them out. By appending only the summary request, approximately 99% of prompts can be served from cache.
The extension also compacts just before the cache expires, so subsequent messages avoid the overhead of re-caching the entire session. This design improves token efficiency for Pi users.
developments.why_it_matters: Users achieve ~99% prompt cache hit rates during compaction, reducing redundant token processing and lowering compute costs per message. The approach allows efficient caching without discarding essential context elements.

external_links.title: GitHub - nicobailon/pi-cached-compaction: Pi compaction that reads the conversation's prompt cache, with a cache-expiry timer · GitHub

developments.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to Agentic AI Foundation
detail: Anthropic announced that it is donating the Agent Skills framework, originally created as an experiment in Claude Code, to the Agentic AI Foundation. The donation follows the earlier transfer of the MCP project and comes as the standard is already integrated into over 70 agent platforms such as ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code.
developments.why_it_matters: Making Agent Skills openly available accelerates its adoption across the expanding ecosystem of AI agents, allowing developers to build on a shared, community‑maintained standard.

developments.title: Linux kernel SMB vulnerability reported at CVSS 9.0
detail: Hensen Juang reported a Linux kernel SMB vulnerability with a CVSS score of 9.0.
No CVE identifier, affected kernel versions, exploit impact, or patch status is provided.
developments.why_it_matters: The 9.0 rating marks critical severity, but the missing technical and remediation details leave administrators unable to determine exposure or select a fix from this report.

developments.title: Vercel's --temporary deploy flag issues a domain that lives for only about an hour
detail: Guillermo Rauch highlighted the `vercel deploy --temporary` command in Vercel's CLI, calling the resulting throwaway deployment workflow 'wild', and in the same post he also singled out Vercel's 'ultrafast ai' as similarly impressive. Malte Ubl's commentary on the exchange underlines the mechanics: you can claim the Vercel domain today, and then keep it for an hour before it disappears.

The linked Vercel page brands the platform as 'Agentic Infrastructure', the 'autonomous stack for every app and agent', placing these short-lived domains within the agent-facing deployment story Vercel is marketing.
developments.why_it_matters: Deployments launched with this flag need no manual teardown because the command's domain stops resolving within roughly an hour, meaning anything shared from a `--temporary` link must be relied on only while it is still live.

developments.title: New pstack companion skill draws agent statecharts with Pele and checks them against formal verification specs
detail: Lauren announced a new companion skill in development for pstack, designed to help agents draw statecharts and then check those diagrams against the specs created with the /create-formal-verification-skill. In the quoted post, she describes the intended workflow: an agent draws a statechart, and the formal verification skill finds bugs through something like TLA+, clarifying how the code and user flows actually behave while catching issues before users run into them. The diagram rendering now uses Pele from Kepano, which she credits for the polished look of the output.
The skill has not shipped yet; she notes that a release is coming soon.
developments.why_it_matters: Pairing agent-drawn statecharts with TLA+-style formal verification makes bug-finding a visual, agent-run step, so user-flow defects surface in the diagram rather than in front of users. As a companion to the existing pstack formal-verification workflow, it extends that setup with concrete diagram output instead of adding a separate toolchain.

developments.title: Grok Bot can now operate native phone apps like Calendar, Reminders, and Contacts
detail: Grok Bot announced a new capability letting it use Calendar, Reminders, Contacts, and more apps directly on a user's phone, with the rollout live now on both iOS and Android. This moves the bot's actions beyond its own chat interface and into the native applications already installed on the device.
Lauren shared the announcement to encourage using the bot with native phone apps.
developments.why_it_matters: The bot now performs tasks at the source in the calendar, reminders, and contacts already on a user's device, so phone-native actions are part of what the agent delivers today on iOS and Android rather than an experiment.

developments.title: Grok Bot 0.75.2 adds report, memo, dashboard and video generation capabilities
detail: Grok Bot version 0.75.2 was released, bringing the ability for the assistant to create and maintain pages such as reports, memos, and dashboards.
The update also introduces new desktop‑chat cards and enables the bot to produce videos from textual descriptions or images.
developments.why_it_matters: These features let users generate structured documents and multimedia directly from the assistant, expanding Grok Bot’s role as a productivity and content‑creation tool.

developments.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash Model Weights Released Publicly
detail: MiniMax announced that the Flash version of its M3.1 model is now publicly available, with a total of 428 billion parameters and 23 billion active per token.
The model shows a generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, and cybersecurity, achieving scores such as 76.2 on BankerToolBench and 82.2 on CyberGym.
MiniMax also highlighted efficiency improvements via Sparse Attention and DSpark speculative decoding.
developments.why_it_matters: Public access to the MiniMax M3.1 Flash weights enables developers to run the model locally and evaluate its strong agentic and security performance without relying on proprietary APIs.

developments.title: Decisions API Reaches GA and OpenResponses Joins Linux Foundation
detail: The Decisions API has entered General Availability, allowing developers to integrate it into production workloads.
OpenResponses announced its membership in the Linux Foundation, signaling broader community support and collaboration.
developments.why_it_matters: GA status enables immediate production use of the Decisions API, while OpenResponses’ Linux Foundation membership can accelerate open‑source contributions and ecosystem growth.
